text: Final Impressions: The Medal Master achivement appears, presently, to be unachiveable, as no medals seem to be produced from bot matches and there are insufficient players for proper pvp/quick matches. The issue with speed vs. fire rate for several weapons still seems to apply (not a lag issue) and this is unfortunate and makes, at least for me, a handful of the weapons totally useless. I would recommend this game if it were picked up in a bundle and/or certainly if it becomes free. As a standalone purchase however, this game has an insufficient player base to justify the expense. I suggest to the developers: 1. Hold some Nexuiz events to better market this older title 2. Decrease the stand-alone price and/or add in some additional DLC (between your more active projects) to increase it's cost vs. benefit rating 3. Actively seek to include the title in other bundles to increase availability and perhaps expand the player base (I acquired the game via the Cryengine dev pack on Humble bundle for example). I am changing the rating on this review to a positive one--as I do find myself playing the game and that, unto itself, speaks volumes. Third impressions: Nexuiz is slowly growing on me. No real online multi-player (lack of population). Still having issues with aiming--given run/jump speeds etc. I have yet to receive any medals--so I believe this remains glitched and may have to be worked around for the achivement to trigger for pokemon purposes. Fun for short bursts, but still can't recommend it as an individual purchase at this time. Second impressions: CTF is definately the best match type so far--such has remained enjoyable. Hitbox/accuracy remains an issue--the raw/base movement of characters still seems to surpass actual projectile speed (does not seem to be a lag/graphic setting issue, but more play is needed). Mutators are enjoyable and afford an excellent, and in a couple instances--funny, variation to some of the other arena games I have played. Tried some online quick matches. Player population remains very limited. One game was fine (albeit a loss) the other has me questioning how prevalent hacking is amonst the minute player base (1-2 shot kills 8 times in a row within 10s of respawning, and whilst on the run, seems a tad high--but then I am new to this product. However, such was not noticed in any bot matches or my other online/pvp matches to date). First impressions: Acquired via the Cryengine Humble Bundle. Maps are generally well designed. CTF is fun, however, DM is, unfortunately, quite bland. Both CTF and DM suffer, from what is intended to be a feature, by the ADHD style of movement within Nexuiz. Yes it is fast paced, but so much so that it is more about "spray and pray" than actual aiming/accuracy. The frequency of powerups/drops et al. is also very high on the maps I've explored to date. This makes resource conservation of little value, thus far, and further supports the "spray and pray" style. If you want arena combat, akin to Speedy gonzales running around with a rocket launcher, then Nexuiz fits the bill. I remain hopeful I'll see some value, beyond achievement collecting, in Nexuiz and I will update this review accordingly as additional play time is logged.

title: no man's sky
text: I wasn't overly fond of this game when it launched, but with the last few updates culminating with 1.3, I am forced to admit... It's become a pretty compelling experience. Just go into it knowing it's a survival game, at its root. But the UI's a lot less frustrating, and the camera mode is great. I hope they continue to improve the (currently super-minimalistic) multiplayer functionality. Haven't tried it yet, but I will eventually. Watching various tutorials helped my appreciation of NMS. Learning how to find and repair crashed ships was a huge help.

title: no man's sky
text: When the game first loads, you fly through the actual game map of the giant galaxy you start in. Each star has planets that are procedurally generated with different terrain, animals, vegetation and it’s really cool to see what the procgen cooks up. You start with a crashed ship and no memory. It is up to repair it using only the resources around you. Finally blasting into space with no loading screen is really fun and never gets old. Throughout your explorations, you never know if you will land on an extreme planet and be hunted by robots, be blasted out of space, or find a paradise full of dinosaurs. The art style and music in this game are both amazing. The story and lore of this game are interesting and I am really into it. It is delivered in adventure game style text. This may be a turn off for some but it reads like a great sci-fi novel. I like this because of the nostalgic feel and greater depth that written word provides. Know what you are getting into though. As you aim to upgrade your weapon, ship, and suit there are times where you could fall into a pattern. Few upgrades are required to enjoy the game but if you are obsessed with upgrading everything NOW you could feel a grind. There are different ways to gain money, blueprints, and better ships so you can mix it up and have fun. For now, I think the game would be more enjoyed by the chill explorer rather than someone looking for a fps slaughter, though the space battles and combat can get crazy. It is definitely not primarily a space shoot 'em up. I have not played survival mode (hard mode) yet and I hear that can get really intense though. I wouldn't recommend this game for young kids as there is mining and inventory management that is typical of a survival game (gets easier with upgrades), and the text that they may be too young to appreciate. Importantly, this game is being updated consistently by the devs. The love they have for the game is clear. Check out some of their GDC lectures on Youtube to see what I mean. The latest update was huge and has been really fun. The initial release was controversial but the game is now really solid. I am around 70 hours in now and still feel like there is so much more to discover. The community is great and has even grouped together at the galactic hub in game. I really think this a very special, stand out game. If it sounds like your type of thing, I do recommend it. Also check out the NMS subreddit if you need more research. Edit: I finished the story that came with the last update. I never expected to care about the characters in a sandboxy game like this. I became invested in the story and the ending impacts your game, although the journey is better than the goal, and leaves you to continue to explore the game afterwards. I can't wait to see what else they do with the game. There is huge potential here.
